proposed_fix.description: Verify the CPU saturation and error spike on adservice, then, with human approval, raise the adservice container's CPU limit modestly and gate the change on error and CPU recovery.
steps: Check adservice pod CPU usage against its requests and limits, and check the container_cpu_cfs_throttled periods metric, to confirm saturation or throttling.
Check whether the app is performing normally: inspect adservice logs and recent deploys or config changes around the onset of the errors (E1, E2).
Review whether CPU requests match actual usage and adjust them if they are clearly mismatched.
With approval, raise the CPU limit on the adservice container only (requests can stay the same) in a small increment, e.g. 25-50%.
Watch adservice_cpu, adservice_error and latency-90 for 10-15 minutes; if there is no improvement, stop escalating and investigate the application (hot loop, bad release, traffic surge) instead.
Check the node kernel version, as R3 suggests, if throttling persists despite adequate limits.
preconditions: Confirm the node has spare allocatable CPU for a higher limit.
Confirm the adservice errors are not caused by an upstream or dependency failure or a recent bad deploy; a rollback would be the better fix in that case.
Record the current CPU requests, limits and replica count.
Get on-call engineer approval before any change is applied.
proposed_fix.rollback: Restore the previously recorded CPU limit (e.g. kubectl rollout undo on the deployment or re-apply the prior manifest) and confirm the pods return to the earlier spec.

contradictions.step: The alert is purely informative and unless there is some other issue with the application, it can be skipped.
contradictions.why: adservice has a concurrent error spike (z=20.0) and latency deviation, and E2 shows a 98% error rate, so there is another issue with the application and the alert cannot be skipped.
